evidence.quote: The operator credential grants access to the two shipping operations.
It does not grant a shell account or access to arbitrary host files.
A credential holder can choose archive entries and receipt labels.
An operator is not authorized to change the renderer program.
An operator is not authorized to write outside the workspace root.
Archive ownership between authenticated operators is deliberately shared.
The service executes as a dedicated Unix account.
The writable roots are administrator provisioned, with no preexisting symlinks.
No container, MAC profile, or read-only root filesystem is supplied.
The service account has ordinary host filesystem permissions.

elm_fir.assessment: Credential, body control, Unix execution, trusted program, bounded workspace authority and absence of symlink setup are retained. Outside-root writes remain conditional on actual service-account permissions. General permission to print labels is not permission to execute commands; removing the explicit shell-injection sentence does not remove that boundary. Corresponding fir README is identical.

evidence.quote: The relay process can write the entire configured document tree.
These gateway behaviors are deployment requirements, not supplied gateway code.
A typical contributor has access to one project, such as `alpha`.
That user can choose any ordinary JSON fields in the forwarded body.
Membership in one project does not grant access to other projects.
The gateway is required to forward operation JSON without authorization-aware rewriting.
The deployment does not supply per-project operating system permissions.
One authenticated project must not overwrite another project's documents.
The production allowlist contains `assets.example.test` only.
The source policy permits HTTP and HTTPS with default ports.
The host may be able to reach private HTTP services on its network.
Whether a particular sensitive private endpoint exists is deployment dependent.
The data tree is administrator provisioned without user-created symlinks.

hawthorn_juniper.assessment: A legitimate alpha-only user is still a valid concrete instance of the general contributor contract. Legacy destination/remote are explicitly documented as repeat fields; they do not grant new project or host permissions. Shared storage and arbitrary forwarded JSON retain the source-proven composition attack; actual sensitive-network impact remains conditional. Corresponding juniper README is identical.

answer_leakage_and_noise.retained_content_assessment: Basic identifier/URL rejection tests, same-value legacy compatibility tests, quoted-label acceptance and blocked erase tests are plausible ordinary coverage. They identify API semantics and a blocked near miss, but do not supply the target mismatch exploit or require a failing security-regression test in the vulnerable fixtures. Operational material about release packaging, retention, recovery, renderer images, supervisors, DNS and external audit is plausible context rather than an answer roadmap. Claims about absent external integrations are not treated as verified deployments.
remaining_difficulty_limits: README still describes architecture, production launch selection, allowed tools and explicit security contracts. That is useful source context and can make resolution easier; it is not a blind real-world audit.
The attack chains span real entrypoint/configuration/service/adapter boundaries, but each function and transform remains short. File count and operational prose alone do not prove depth.
Fixed paired cases can reveal the exact correction if a reviewer sees both trees together. Candidate evaluation should isolate cases as intended; this key audit necessarily compared them.
Accepting fixture construction does not predict reviewer success, model ranking or robustness. Those require the planned empirical runs.

optional_surviving_caveats.detail: fir authentication_surface still says 'both findings'; juniper identity_boundary still references 'Composition findings'. Empty must_find and explicit fixed guards resolve intended semantics. These were not part of the revision scope.

request.setTimeout(2000) is socket inactivity timeout, not a total two-second deadline. Keys claim timeout without a total-time guarantee. Decoded UTF-8 response accumulation is bounded by abort-on-crossing logic, not every raw network allocation or wire byte. No extra resource-exhaustion exploit is proved.

evidence.quote: The last completed write determines the contents of an overlapping filename.

optional_surviving_caveats.detail: The preceding statement correctly says there is no cross-request workspace lock. This following sentence is stronger than writeFile guarantees for concurrent same-file operations; overlapping writes need not provide clean last-completion-wins semantics. This does not change planted keys or require adding a concurrency finding under their intended scope. Same prose in fir.

juniper remote equality is against normalized approved.url, so a differently spelled equivalent repeated raw URL can be rejected. Revised happy-path test explicitly repeats the normalized source. No policy bypass follows.
